narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Return to Achilles’ answer among the dead: he prefers humble life to kingship over the departed. This is a literary encounter with a remembered hero; it is not by itself evidence of a particular community’s hero-cult ritual.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translation; whitespace normalized): “are dead.’ “‘Say not a word,’ he answered, ‘in death’s favour; I would rather be a paid servant in a poor man’s house and be above ground than king of kings among the dead. But give me news about my son; is he gone to the wars and will he be a great soldier, or is this not so? Tell me also if you have”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Interpretation: The living hero gains direction by listening to those whose stories complicate his own.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: A literary encounter with a dead hero establishes what this poem stages. A historical claim about hero cult would require evidence about a particular community’s sanctuary, offerings, and practices.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: The dead make the heroic past answerable to the present.
